Why the Quran is from God

Justice even against yourself

The Quran commands fairness against yourself and your family, and toward a people you dislike.

What would a tribal leader ask of his followers? Loyalty to their own. The Quran asks for justice even against yourself, your parents and your relatives, and it says hatred of a people must not make you unfair. It forbids killing children and answers the fear of poverty behind it. It makes the orphan and the hungry a test of faith. Honour lies in God-consciousness, not in a tribe.

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوِ ٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ۚ إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا ۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ وَإِن تَلْوُۥٓا۟ أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allāh, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allāh is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allāh is ever, of what you do, Aware.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:135

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allāh, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allāh; indeed, Allāh is [fully] Aware of what you do.

Quran · Al-Ma'idah 5:8

﴿وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَـٰدَكُمْ خَشْيَةَ إِمْلَـٰقٍ ۖ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُهُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ قَتْلَهُمْ كَانَ خِطْـًٔا كَبِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:31

﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُۥدَةُ سُئِلَتْ٨ بِأَىِّ ذَنۢبٍ قُتِلَتْ٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked For what sin she was killed

Quran · At-Takwir 81:8-9

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ١ فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ٢ وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? For that is the one who drives away the orphan And does not encourage the feeding of the poor.

Quran · Al-Ma'un 107:1-3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَـٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَـٰكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Aware.

Quran · Al-Hujurat 49:13

You might ask

QuestionDidn't other traditions teach justice too?
AnswerThey did, and the Quran expects that. It says a messenger came to every people. Finding this elsewhere is what one message looks like.Quran · An-Nahl 16:36
QuestionDoesn't the Quran also have hard verses?
AnswerIt does, on women, slaves and war. They deserve an honest reading, not silence, and the questions linked below face them. Here the point is what is plainly commanded.Quran · An-Nisa 4:135
QuestionDoes a high moral command show a divine source?
AnswerNot alone. Decent people reach far on their own. It shows a moral vision that asks more of you than your tribe does, and that is worth weighing.Quran · Al-Ma'idah 5:8

Justice that costs you something: that is the kind the Quran asks for.
